ORAL:
1.
By virtue of a common award dated 24.04.2010, three claim petitions came to be decided by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kathua (for short the Tribunal).

One claim petition, titled, "Om Parkash vs Vinod Kumar and others" was filed by Om Parkash for grant of compensation on account of death of his son, who was the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No. Pb06-2359.

sentences.text: Second claim petition was filed by Ajay Kumar titled, "Ajay Kumar vs Vinod Kumar and others", for grant of compensation on account of injuries suffered by him and the third claim petition was filed by Ajay Kumar and his children titled "Ajay Kumar and others vs Vinod Kumar and others" for grant of compensation on account of death of Saroj Puri, who was the wife of Ajay Kumar and mother of other claimants.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petition filed by Om Parkash was dismissed by the learned Tribunal and the other two claim petitions were allowed by the learned Tribunal and compensation of Rs. 3,99,000/- and Rs. 70,000/- was granted in favour of claimant Ajay Kumar and his children & Ajay Kumar respectively.

The owners i.e. the appellants were fastened with liability to satisfy the award, as the driver of vehicle bearing No. Pb06-2359 was found to be negligent while driving the vehicle and the injured claimant and the deceased were travelling in the offending vehicle i.e. Truck bearing No. PB06-2359 as gratuitous passengers.

2. The appellants, who are the co-owners of the vehicle bearing No. PB06- 2359, through the medium of these two appeals, have assailed the award MA Nos. 708/2010 &
710/2010 dated 24.04.2010 passed by the learned Tribunal in the two claim petitions, one preferred by Ajay Kumar individually and the other along with his children.

3. The appellants have contended that the learned tribunal has not appreciated the evidence in its right perspective and the award, if it was required to be passed, the same was to be satisfied by the insurance company.
Charanjit Kumar vs Ajay Kumar S/O. Sh. Om Parkash on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3122552/
3 4.

Mr. Anirudh Sharma, learned counsel for the appellants has argued that once the learned Tribunal did not believe the testimony of the eyewitness, the Tribunal could not have fastened the liability upon the owners/appellants merely placing reliance upon the FIR.

He has further submitted that the deceased driver acted beyond the scope of his employment as such, the appellants could not have been made liable for the unauthorized act of the driver of the appellants.
5. Heard and perused the record.

6. The claimant-Ajay Kumar filed a claim petition for grant of compensation in respect of injuries suffered by him, and he along with others filed another claim petition for grant of compensation on account of death of Saroj Puri who happened to be his wife and the mother of other claimants in a vehicular accident that took place on 18.12.1999 at 23.45 Oclock, when the truck bearing registration No. PB06 2359, being driven by its driver namely Arwan Kumar, was hit by another truck bearing No. HP38 3491 at a place Chhan Rorian, regarding which FIR bearing No. 131/1999 dated 18.12.1999 was registered with Police Station, Rajbagh.

It was stated by the appellants that the deceased Arwan Kumar was driving his MA Nos. 708/2010 & 710/2010 truck Pb06 2359 and deceased-Saroj Puri and one of the claimants, Ajay Kumar, were also with him.

They were going towards Kathua from Jammu and when they reached Chan Rorian, a rash and negligently driven truck bearing No. HP38 3491 came from the opposite side and hit truck bearing No. Pb06-2359, due to which, Arwan Kumar and Saroj Puri died.

Both these claim petitions and third one filed by the father of the deceased driver-Arvan Kumar, driver of vehicle bearing No. PB06 2359 were objected to by Rachpaul Singh i.e. the owner of vehicle HP-38 3491 and it was specifically pleaded by him that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the deceased driver-Arvan Kumar i.e. driver of offending vehicle bearing No. PB06 2359.

The insurer of vehicle bearing No.
HP38 3491 also objected to the claim petition and pleaded that the insurance policy of truck bearing No. HP38 3491 has been cancelled by the insurance company.
The appellants also objected to the claim petitions filed by the claimants by asserting that the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of Truck bearing No. HP38 3491.

The insurance company of Truck bearing No.
PB06 2369 also objected to the claim petition by taking a stand that the deceased Saroj Puri and claimant Ajay Kumar were travelling in the truck as a gratuitous passengers and as such the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation.

7. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues:
1. Whether on 18.1299the respondent no. l drove his vehicle-bearing no. HP38-3491 in a rash and negligent manner and when reached near Chhan Rorian Kathua, MA Nos. 708/2010 & 710/2010 dashed it against the vehicle no. PB06-2359 coming from the opposite direction and driven by deceased Arwan Kumar as a result of which Arwan Kumar and Saroj Puri died whereas the petitioner Ajay Kumar sustained grievous Injuries?

OPP.
2.

Whether the alleged accident has taken place due to the negligent driving of the driver of truck no. PB06-2359and as such the Insurance company is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners?

OPR.

4 3.
In case of proof of Issues 1&2, whether the petitioners are entitled to compensation from the respondents?

OPP. 
4. Whether this Tribunal has no Jurisdiction to try claim petition no. 10?

OPR. 
5. Whether the driver of the offending vehicle no. HP38- 3491 was not holding a valid driving licence?

OPR. 
6. Whether the claim petitions are not maintainable and are liable to be dismissed, as there did not exist any insurance contract between the insurer and the insured at the time of accident?

OPR. 
7.
Whether the petitions are bad for mis-joinder and non- joinder of necessary parties?

OPR. 
8. Relief.
8.
The claimant-Ajay Kumar besides examining himself, also examined Dr. J. P. S. Balla and the claimant in claim petition titled, Om Parkash vs Vinod Kumar and others appeared as his own witness.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In rebuttal, Vinod Kumar, the driver of the vehicle bearing No. HP38 3491 and Rachpal Singh, the owner of the vehicle bearing No. HP38 3491, besides examining themselves also examined Rajesh Thakur, Satpal Sharma, Satish Sharma, Vijay Kumar, as their witnesses.
The evidence of these witnesses shall be discussed as and when required.
9. It is contended by the appellants that once the Tribunal did not believe the statement of eyewitness in respect of the occurrence, no liability could have been fastened upon the appellants.

So far as occurrence is concerned, the claimant-Ajay Kumar in his statement stated that the accident was caused by a truck bearing registration No. HP38 3491 which was being MA Nos. 708/2010 &
710/2010 driven by its driver i.e. Vinod Kumar in a rash and negligent manner due to which he got injured and his brother Arwan Kumar and his wife Saroj Puri died on spot.

The learned Tribunal has disbelieved the statement of the claimant-Ajay Kumar and rightly so because the driver of another vehicle bearing registration No. HP38 3491 namely, Vinod Kumar who happened to be the respondent No. 1 in the claim petition appeared as his own witness and stated that on 18.12.1999 he was driving truck bearing No. HP38 3491, which had met with an accident near Chhan Rorian due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle No. PB06 3459 by its driver when the said truck was coming from Jammu side.

It was stated by him that during investigation it was found that the accident took place due to rash and negligence by Arvan Kumar, the driver of Truck bearing No. PB06 2359, who was the brother of claimant Ajay Kumar and son of another claimant Om Parkash.
He further stated that the matter was re-investigated by the Police and again it was found that the Arvan Kumar was negligent while driving the vehicle which resulted into an accident.
He also stated that father-Om Parkash one of the claimants had filed a complaint against him in the court at Hiranagar, wherein he was acquitted.

Sat Pal Sharma, Investigating Officer in his deposition stated that as per his investigation, driver of Truck bearing No. HP38-3491 was not found responsible for accident and Charanjit Kumar vs Ajay Kumar S/O. Sh. Om Parkash on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3122552/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5 driver of Truck No. PB06-2359 drove the vehicle negligently.
Both these witnesses were relied upon by the learned Tribunal to return a finding that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of deceased Arvan Kumar.

In view of the categoric statements made by Vinod Kumar and Sat Pal Sharma, IO, that the accident took place because of rash and negligent driving of Arvan Kumar, the finding of the learned Tribunal in respect of the negligence of Arvan Kumar while driving the vehicle PB06 2359 on the date of accident, cannot be faulted with.
Therefore, the contention of the appellants is found to be without any merit, the same is rejected.
11. It was next contended by the appellant that the driver acted beyond the scope of his employment and caused the accident therefore, no liability could have been fastened upon the appellants.
This fact is established from the record that the claimant-Ajay Kumar and his wife Saroj Puri were travelling in the vehicle PB06-2359 as gratuitous passengers.

Once they were travelling in the vehicle as gratuitous passengers, the appellants cannot be exonerated of their liability by asserting that the driver engaged by them exceeded his authority and put the vehicle to unauthorized use.
This contention too, is without any force and as such is rejected.
12. In view of the above, this Court does not find any infirmity in the award impugned in both these appeals.
Accordingly, both the appeals are dismissed being devoid of any merit.
13. Record of the Tribunal be sent back, if received in original.
(RAJNESH OSWAL) JUDGE Jammu 08.10.2024 Rakesh
